$description: #236-R1 principle register. Statements are the lane's OWN WORDS (<=25 words), never the source's. Every evidence URL was fetched on 2026-09-02 or is explicitly marked NOT FETCHED / UNPROVEN. Grades: A quantitative law, B replicated effect, C expert heuristic, D contested/folk, L legal requirement.

grade_ladder.C: expert heuristic, wide consensus, thin direct experiment
grade_ladder.L: legal or regulatory requirement, not a heuristic

principles.statement: Time to hit a target grows with distance and shrinks with target size, by a logarithmic relation that predicts real numbers.
principles.evidence: Fitts 1954, J Exp Psychol, 'The information capacity of the human motor system...' — https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1037/h0055392 (fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Rapid aimed movement, one dimension, mouse/stylus/finger; derived from tapping and disc-transfer tasks, not reading or decision tasks.
principles.known_misreadings: Read as 'make buttons big'. It predicts TIME, not preference; and it says nothing about whether the target should exist.
principles.refutation_probe: Extension fetched: Bi, Li & Zhai 2013 'FFitts law' https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1145/2470654.2466180 — finger touch needs a modified model. MacKenzie 1992 Shannon formulation https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1207/s15327051hci0701_3. No refutation found; the model is extended, not overturned.

principles.statement: Choice reaction time rises with the logarithm of the number of equally likely alternatives.
principles.grade_alt: A for the lab effect, D for the menu application
principles.grade_reason: The law itself is replicated and predictive; its transfer to menus is the contested part and should be graded separately.
principles.evidence: Hick 1952 'On the Rate of Gain of Information' https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1080/17470215208416600; Hyman 1953 https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1037/h0056940 (both fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Simple forced choice with equiprobable, already-known stimuli and practised participants. NOT visual search of unfamiliar labels.
principles.known_misreadings: Applied to navigation menus as 'fewer items = faster'. Menu use is visual search plus decision; the law covers only the decision half.
principles.refutation_probe: Landauer & Nachbar 1985 menu breadth/depth https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1145/1165385.317470 and Cockburn, Gutwin & Greenberg 2007 predictive menu model https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1145/1240624.1240723 (both fetched) — menu performance needs search terms Hick does not contain.

principles.statement: Time to move through a constrained path grows with path length divided by path width — a tunnel, not a target.
principles.evidence: Accot & Zhai 1997 'Beyond Fitts' law' CHI https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1145/258549.258760 (fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Continuous trajectory tasks: cascading menus, sliders, drawing. Desktop pointing devices.
principles.known_misreadings: Ignored entirely; most designers do not know cascading submenus have a measurable cost model.
principles.refutation_probe: No refutation found via Crossref bibliographic query; the law is extended rather than contested.

principles.statement: Interaction time can be predicted before building anything by summing keystroke, pointing, homing and mental operators.
principles.evidence: Card, Moran & Newell 1980, CACM https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1145/358886.358895 (fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Error-free expert performance on routine tasks. Says nothing about learning, errors or satisfaction.
principles.known_misreadings: Treated as obsolete. It is the only method that prices a flow before a pixel is drawn.
principles.refutation_probe: No refutation search run beyond Crossref lookup; the known limit (expert, error-free) is stated in the original.

principles.statement: Speed and accuracy trade against each other; a design that makes an action faster usually makes it likelier to be wrong.
principles.evidence: Wickelgren 1977 'Speed-accuracy tradeoff and information processing dynamics' https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1016/0001-6918(77)90012-9 (fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Perceptual-motor and decision tasks generally; the shape of the curve is task-specific.
principles.known_misreadings: Optimising a funnel for speed while reporting error rate separately, as if the two were independent.
principles.refutation_probe: No refutation found; this is a foundational constraint, not a claim in dispute.

principles.statement: People judge position on a common scale far more accurately than angle, area or colour saturation.
principles.grade_reason: Experimental and replicated, with an ordinal ranking rather than a closed-form predictive equation — it sits on the A/B border.
principles.evidence: Cleveland & McGill 1984, JASA https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1080/01621459.1984.10478080 (fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Static 2D statistical graphics, accuracy of magnitude judgement. Not aesthetic preference, not memorability.
principles.known_misreadings: Used to ban pie charts outright. The finding is an accuracy ranking, not a prohibition.
principles.refutation_probe: No refutation search beyond Crossref; later work (Heer & Bostock) is replication, not refutation — NOT fetched in this lane.

principles.statement: An item that differs from its neighbours is remembered better than the items it sits among.
principles.evidence: PRIMARY NOT FETCHED. Secondary receipt: lawsofux.com/ (fetched) 'the one that differs from the rest is most likely to be remembered'
principles.scope_conditions: List learning of verbal items; extended to visual salience in interfaces without direct interface replication being fetched here.
principles.known_misreadings: Used to justify one loud element per screen. It predicts MEMORY, not comprehension or click-through.
principles.refutation_probe: Von Restorff 1933 has no DOI retrievable via Crossref; primary is UNPROVEN in this lane. The effect's textbook status is not a substitute for the paper.

principles.statement: People recall the first and last items in a sequence better than the middle ones.
principles.evidence: Murdock 1962 'The serial position effect of free recall' https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1037/h0045106 (fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Free recall of word lists. Interface transfer (nav bars, list ordering) is an analogy, not a replication.
principles.known_misreadings: Read as 'put the important nav item last'. Recall of a word list is not a click on a visible menu.
principles.refutation_probe: No interface-level replication fetched. Declared gap.

principles.statement: People judge a past experience mostly by its most intense moment and its ending, not by its total duration.
principles.evidence: Redelmeier & Kahneman 1996, Pain https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1016/0304-3959(96)02994-6 (fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Painful medical procedures and short affective episodes. Duration neglect is the mechanism.
principles.known_misreadings: Used to justify a delightful confirmation screen while the middle of the journey stays broken.
principles.refutation_probe: Boundary-condition work fetched: Do, Rupert & Wolford 2008 'Evaluations of pleasurable experiences: the peak-end rule' https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1037/e527352012-042 — the rule holds less cleanly for pleasant experiences than painful ones.

principles.statement: People rate attractive interfaces as easier to use, and that impression survives some real usability problems.
principles.evidence: Kurosu & Kashimura 1995 CHI https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1145/223355.223680; Tractinsky, Katz & Ikar 2000 'What is beautiful is usable' https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1016/S0953-5438(00)00031-X (both fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: ATM layouts (1995, Japan) and their replication (2000, Israel); perceived usability ratings, not task completion.
principles.known_misreadings: Cited as 'beauty makes things usable'. It makes things FEEL usable — which is exactly the honesty problem.
principles.refutation_probe: Critical replications fetched: Tuch, Roth & Hornbaek 2012 https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1016/j.chb.2012.03.024 finds the relation weaker and asymmetric; Sonderegger & Sauer 2010 https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1016/j.apergo.2009.09.002 finds aesthetics affects performance under some conditions. The effect survives but shrinks.

principles.statement: Working memory holds about four chunks, not seven; the classic seven came from tasks that allowed rehearsal.
principles.evidence: Cowan 2001 'The magical number 4 in short-term memory' BBS https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1017/S0140525X01003922 (fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Capacity measured when rehearsal and chunking are blocked; adults, laboratory tasks.
principles.known_misreadings: Swapped in as a new magic number for menu length. It is a capacity claim about held items, not about visible options.
principles.refutation_probe: This IS the refutation of Miller 1956 https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1037/h0043158 (fetched). The correction is 25 years old and still not in most design lists.

principles.statement: Grouping information into meaningful units lets people hold and act on more of it than the raw items alone.
principles.evidence: Miller 1956, Psychological Review https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1037/h0043158 (fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Verbal and digit material; the chunk must be meaningful TO THE USER, which is domain-dependent.
principles.known_misreadings: Confused with the 7±2 capacity claim. Chunking is the durable finding; the number is not.
principles.refutation_probe: Cowan 2001 https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1017/S0140525X01003922 (fetched) revises the capacity, not the chunking mechanism.

principles.statement: Working memory is limited, so effort spent on the interface itself is effort unavailable for the task.
principles.evidence: Sweller 1988 'Cognitive Load During Problem Solving' Cognitive Science https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1207/s15516709cog1202_4 (fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Instructional problem-solving in learners; extraneous vs intrinsic load. Transfer to expert tool use is an extension.
principles.known_misreadings: Used to justify removing content. The theory distinguishes extraneous load (remove) from intrinsic load (cannot remove).
principles.refutation_probe: Cognitive load theory has an active internal critique literature (measurement validity) NOT fetched in this lane. Declared gap.

principles.statement: Unfinished tasks stay in mind more readily than finished ones.
principles.grade_reason: The 1927 original is not retrievable and the replication record is mixed; graded B for its influence but a D case is defensible.
principles.evidence: PRIMARY NOT FETCHED (1927, no retrievable DOI). Later treatment fetched: Seifert & Patalano 1991 'Memory for interrupted problems: The Zeigarnik effect revisited' https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1037/e665402011-235
principles.scope_conditions: Interrupted laboratory tasks; effect size and conditions are unstable across the later literature.
principles.known_misreadings: Used to justify progress bars and 'you're 60% done' nags of any kind. The effect is about memory, not motivation.
principles.refutation_probe: Search recorded: Crossref bibliographic query for a Zeigarnik replication returned only a 1991 revisit, not a modern replication. Weak base, declared.

principles.statement: Effort toward a goal increases as the goal gets closer, and artificial head starts can trigger the same acceleration.
principles.originator: Hull; revived by Kivetz et al.
principles.evidence: Kivetz, Urminsky & Zheng 2006 'The Goal-Gradient Hypothesis Resurrected' JMR https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1509/jmkr.43.1.39 (fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Coffee-card loyalty programmes and song-rating tasks; real purchase acceleration measured.
principles.known_misreadings: Confused with the Zeigarnik effect. Also the 'illusionary progress' finding is the one with ethical teeth.
principles.refutation_probe: The 2006 paper is itself the replication of a much older animal-learning claim; no refutation fetched.

principles.statement: People choose navigation paths the way animals forage: by the strongest cue that the target lies that way.
principles.evidence: Pirolli & Card 1999 'Information foraging' Psychological Review https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1037/0033-295X.106.4.643 (fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Information-seeking in large corpora; formal model with measurable scent and patch-leaving predictions.
principles.known_misreadings: Not misread so much as unknown — practitioners reach for the three-click rule instead, which has no model at all.
principles.refutation_probe: No refutation found. This theory is the evidence-backed replacement for the folk click-count rules.

principles.statement: People take a cue about what to do from what similar others are doing, measurably more than from abstract appeals.
principles.evidence: Goldstein, Cialdini & Griskevicius 2008 'A Room with a Viewpoint' JCR https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1086/586910 (fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Hotel towel-reuse field experiments; descriptive norms matched to the immediate setting worked best.
principles.known_misreadings: Generalised into fabricated urgency and fake counts — which the DSA now prohibits.
principles.refutation_probe: Cialdini's own site could not be fetched (SSL name mismatch on influenceatwork.com); the field experiment stands in its place.

principles.statement: Losses loom larger than equivalent gains, so framing an identical outcome as a loss changes the decision.
principles.evidence: Kahneman & Tversky 1979 'Prospect Theory' Econometrica https://api.crossref.org/works/10.2307/1914185 (fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Monetary gambles with stated probabilities. Magnitude in interfaces is unestablished.
principles.known_misreadings: Used to justify confirmshaming ('No thanks, I hate saving money') — a named deceptive pattern.
principles.refutation_probe: Loss aversion has a live replication debate (Gal & Rucker) NOT fetched in this lane. Declared gap.

principles.statement: People attend to a subset of what is present, usually the part matching their current goal, and miss the rest.
principles.evidence: PRIMARY NOT FETCHED. Secondary receipt: lawsofux.com/ (fetched) 'focusing our attention only to a subset of stimuli'
principles.scope_conditions: Attentional laboratory tasks and inattentional-blindness demonstrations; interface transfer via banner blindness studies not fetched here.
principles.known_misreadings: Used to argue for more salience everywhere, which destroys the contrast the effect depends on.
principles.refutation_probe: No primary fetched. Declared gap: this row is currently secondary-only.

principles.statement: Operators must perceive the elements, understand what they mean, and project what happens next; displays succeed or fail at those three.
principles.evidence: Endsley 1995 'Toward a Theory of Situation Awareness in Dynamic Systems' Human Factors https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1518/001872095779049543 (fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Aviation and process-control operators; high-tempo monitoring tasks.
principles.known_misreadings: Absent from commercial design practice entirely — yet a trading or ops dashboard is exactly this problem.
principles.refutation_probe: Endsley's model has a known critique from distributed-cognition authors NOT fetched here. Declared gap.

principles.statement: Two tasks interfere most when they compete for the same perceptual channel; splitting across channels reduces interference.
principles.evidence: Wickens 2002 'Multiple resources and performance prediction' TIES https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1080/14639220210123806 (fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Dual-task workload prediction in applied settings.
principles.known_misreadings: Used to justify adding sound or haptics without measuring whether the channel is already loaded.
principles.refutation_probe: No refutation fetched.

principles.statement: Perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use predict whether people will actually adopt a system.
principles.evidence: Davis 1989, MIS Quarterly https://api.crossref.org/works/10.2307/249008 (fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Organisational software adoption, self-report instruments. Predicts intention better than sustained use.
principles.known_misreadings: Ignored by designers, over-relied on by procurement. Usefulness usually beats ease, which inverts a lot of design effort.
principles.refutation_probe: Widely replicated and widely criticised for tautology; the critique literature was NOT fetched. Declared gap.

principles.statement: Showing the work a system is doing can make a wait feel more valuable, sometimes beating an instant result.
principles.evidence: Buell & Norton 2011 'The Labor Illusion' Management Science https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1287/mnsc.1110.1376 (fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Travel-search websites; perceived value and satisfaction, not task time.
principles.known_misreadings: Used to justify fake loading spinners generally. The effect depended on the work shown being real and legible.
principles.refutation_probe: No refutation fetched. NOTE this is the direct empirical counterweight to 'always be faster'.

principles.statement: Two trained evaluators applying the same heuristic list to the same interface find substantially different problems.
principles.evidence: Hertzum & Jacobsen 2001 'The Evaluator Effect' IJHCI https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1207/s15327590ijhc1304_05 (fetched); Molich & Dumas 2008 CUE-4 https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1080/01449290600959062 (fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Usability inspection and testing methods across multiple professional teams.
principles.known_misreadings: Not a misreading but an omission: heuristic scores are reported as if they were measurements.
principles.refutation_probe: This IS the refutation family. It is the strongest reason no heuristic list can be graded above C.

principles.statement: Testing with five users is not a general law; the right number depends on the problem-discovery rate, which varies.
principles.evidence: Faulkner 2003 'Beyond the five-user assumption' Behavior Research Methods https://api.crossref.org/works/10.3758/bf03195514 (fetched)
principles.scope_conditions: Monte Carlo resampling of a 60-user study; five users found between 55% and 99% of problems depending on which five.
principles.known_misreadings: 'Five users find 85% of problems' quoted as if the variance were zero. The variance is the finding.
principles.refutation_probe: Faulkner is the refutation; also Hornbaek 2006 on measurement practice {CR}10.1016/j.ijhcs.2005.06.002 (fetched).
